timing: Immediate post-walk self-report in the studied session.
population: Healthy adult and predominantly young-adult/student samples in specified field settings.
operation: Specified low-intensity natural outdoor walk compared with a time/distance-matched urban or built-setting walk.
scope: Immediate self-reported positive affect or mood-valence component only.
limitations: No enduring mood, clinical benefit, cognition, attention, stress physiology, behavior, dose-response, practitioner recommendation or universal setting transfer. The natural route is a multisensory package.

reason: Task performance and annoyance vary by level, task and source; neither is an exact cognitive-load measure.
The experiment bundles heat and noise; syntheses show task, dose and adaptation dependence, blocking a broad component effect.
Ventilation, VOCs and CO2 are partly bundled; task productivity is not a broad latent capacity and a controlled child trial reports a next-day cognition null.
